text:
acme_ops: hey team, started getting a bunch of reports this morning — users are immediately prompted for MFA again after completing it on web. mobile app sessions seem fine. happening on chrome 118 and safari 17. can we dig? :grimacing:

alex: ugh. any error sample? are they getting a 401 from API or just redirected to /reauth?

acme_ops: they see a redirect loop to the reauth page, then a 401 from /v1/sessions when the app tries to exchange the assertion. no obvious logs on our side; customers reported it after a password change in identity provider. attaching one curl session from a repro user: 

acme_ops: ```
$ curl -i -L -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  'https://app.acme.example.com/auth/callback?state=xyz'

HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=3600
Location: /sso/finish

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{"status":"ok"}
```

marta: interesting — header shows SameSite=None and Secure which is expected. do you have the Set-Cookie for `device_trust`/`mfa_remembered`?

acme_ops: i only captured `session` here. users say their browser shows the session cookie present but the app still triggers reauth. could be our refresh_token rotation or a mismatch in token scopes after password change.

sam: @acme_ops can you grab the network trace for the /v1/sessions exchange? need the request body and response headers. often this is `refresh_token` rejected with `invalid_grant` when idp revoked tokens on password change.

acme_ops: attaching sanitized response: 

acme_ops: ```json
{
  "error": "invalid_grant",
  "error_description": "Refresh token revoked by user (password change)."
}
```

alex: that points to IDP revocation. but why does web keep showing a valid session cookie? two things could be happening: 1) session cookie is a short-lived JWT we accept locally until we verify with introspect endpoint, or 2) there's a separate device-trust cookie with TTL that's longer and not being checked. if cookie is client-only state (not introspected) the UI might think user is logged in while backend rejects API calls.

marta: run a quick local repro: create a session, then revoke refresh token at idp, then call `/v1/generate` or any protected endpoint. check `x-session-verified` header in our gateway logs. i'll paste the grep I use: 

marta: ```bash
grep -i "x-session-verified" /var/log/redwood/gateway/*.log | tail -n 50
```

sam: also check the `kid` on the session JWT and `exp` to verify if cookie expiry is being set in the future incorrectly (timezone/units bug we've seen before).

acme_ops: ran the repro. gateway shows `x-session-verified: false` and downstream returns 401 with body `{"code":"session_invalid","msg":"device trust failed"}`. i can reproduce in chrome by toggling third-party cookie block and disabling SameSite enforcement — seems flaky.

alex: that detail is key — chrome settings + identity provider changes can create a mismatch where browser retains cookie but we can't validate device trust because the `device_assertion` cookie (httponly) isn't sent due to SameSite rules on the cross-site redirect. can you paste the full `Set-Cookie` chain for `device_assertion` if present?

acme_ops: found it. headers: 

acme_ops: ```
Set-Cookie: device_assertion=abc123; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=2592000
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=3600
```

marta: aha — `device_assertion` is SameSite=Lax. when we do the POST-redirect dance on SSO callback (cross-site), Lax blocks the cookie sending on some flows, especially when the redirect includes an interstitial or the IdP uses a POST. that prevents backend from seeing device_assertion and we reject the session. previously we defaulted to `SameSite=None` for device cookies but a recent change in session-service mistakenly set Lax for long-lived device assertions.

alex: creating a quick patch to set `SameSite=None` for `device_assertion` when issuing during SSO flows. in the meantime, workaround is to instruct customers to set cookie policy or use the mobile app. but we need to patch server.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-987 — "device_assertion SameSite misconfigured causing reauth loops after IDP token revocation". Priority: P2. Assigned: sessions-team.

marta: I'm going to backport a hotfix to the session issuer. patch diff: 

marta: ```diff
- set_cookie('device_assertion', token, samesite='Lax')
+ set_cookie('device_assertion', token, samesite='None')
```

sam: also add a migration check to detect any existing device_assertion cookies with wrong attribute and for canary we can emit a warning header `x-device-assertion-samesite=bad` when present so we can find impacted traffic.

acme_ops: thanks. any ETA? we have ~40 affected users across two customers — some are enterprise SSO.

alex: patch merged to branch `fix/device-samesite` and deploying canary to `sessions-canary` in eu-west-1 now. ETA ~30m for canary warmup, 2h for global rollout if no regressions. will post updates here.

marta: rolling out canary. i added the `x-device-assertion-samesite` header to logs and filtered by `user-agent` showing Chrome 118. so far canary looks good for 15m.

acme_ops: can confirm two users from acme that were stuck are now able to complete SSO. they still see old cookie in devtools but no reauth loop. :party_parrot:

marta: excellent. follow-up actions: 
- add integration test asserting `SameSite=None` for device_assertion cookie in SSO flow
- update session-service changelog + note about careful defaults for long-lived cookies
- reach out to impacted customers with explanation and mitigation steps

alex: i'll also file a small runbook entry for support: how to confirm `x-device-assertion-samesite=bad` in logs and the immediate workaround (instruct users to clear site data or use mobile app until fix).

acme_ops: thanks to the team — saving us from a big support surge. will keep monitoring and close INC when global rolled out.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-987 status: Mitigated (canary success). Next: Schedule global rollout (2h window).
